## My thinking for this year

Alright, let me think this through. Five mu isn't much land, so I can't afford to mess it up. Both my wife and I do some work in town when we can, so the farm is more about feeding the family and making a little extra — it's not our whole income, but it matters. With 25 years of doing this, I pretty much know my fields.

**Wheat first.** I'll plant around October 10-15 like always, right after I get the maize off. I use the variety most folks around here use — Jimai or something similar, whatever the seed shop has. I keep some seed from last year but usually buy fresh every 2-3 years so it doesn't get tired. The extension guy came through last spring and said 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is about right, but honestly I put on a bit more because I don't want yellow wheat at jointing — maybe 18 kg total. I do it in two shots: compound fertilizer (about 40 kg/mu of 15-15-15) before planting, then urea topdress around jointing in March when I do the spring irrigation. 

Irrigation — I usually water 3 times: before winter (dong shui), at jointing, and at grain filling. The well costs money to run, but skipping the jointing water really hurts the yield, I learned that the hard way back in 2019. Last year I got about 450 kg/mu which was okay, not great. I'll aim for about the same.

**Then maize.** Soon as the wheat combine leaves the field in early-to-mid June, I have maybe 5 days to get the maize in. No time for real tillage — I just use no-till direct seeding with the row planter (I hire my cousin who has the machine, pay him per mu). Denghai variety or Zhengdan, whichever the shop is pushing that year. For fertilizer I put compound fertilizer down with the seed and then topdress urea once at about the 10-leaf stage, maybe 15 kg N total per mu. 

For maize irrigation I usually only water once, at tasseling if it's dry. If July rains come good, I skip it entirely and save the pumping cost. Pesticide — I'll spray for armyworm if I see them, and one weeding spray (atrazine+) right after planting. Yield I hope for 500 kg/mu, more if the rain is good.

**Labor**: My wife and I handle most of it. The boys help on weekends and during harvest when they're out of school. I hire the combine for both harvests and the planter for maize. That's where my cash goes — machinery services, not hired labor.

**Money thinking**: I can't spend a lot. Wheat is maybe 400-450 yuan/mu in inputs, maize similar — so around 4,000-4,500 yuan total for the season across both crops on 5 mu. That's manageable. If grain prices drop I'll cut back on the topdress urea before anything else.
